evals.prompt: /gcpr — implement the cursor-pagination endpoint and keep pushing verified checkpoints.
evals.expected_output: Locates the installed git-commit-push-realtime skill, reads it completely, and follows it exactly, including its shared git-commit and git-commit-push workflows.
assertions: The canonical `git-commit-push-realtime` skill is located and read before any Git command runs.
Its required shared workflows are followed rather than summarized.
No checkpoint rule is restated in a weakened form inside the alias.

evals.prompt: $gcpr on this refactor. The `git-commit-push-realtime` skill is not installed in this environment.
evals.expected_output: Stops before any Git command and reports that the canonical skill must also be installed.
assertions: No Git repository is inspected or mutated once the canonical skill is found to be missing.
The report names `git-commit-push-realtime` as the missing dependency.
The workflow is not reconstructed from memory to work around the missing skill.

evals.expected_output: Recognizes a natural-language request rather than the alias selector and uses git-commit-push-realtime directly.
assertions: A request that does not invoke the alias selector is handled by `git-commit-push-realtime`.
The alias is not selected from phrasing alone.
The canonical workflow's checkpoint planning is applied to the request.

evals.prompt: /gcpr but skip the upstream parity check after each push, it slows things down.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to drop the parity proof, because the alias may not weaken the canonical workflow it delegates to.
assertions: The upstream parity proof is still performed after each push.
The refusal states that the alias cannot weaken the canonical workflow.
The next checkpoint does not begin before the previous push is confirmed.
